texts: Nearly 60 percent of neonates undergoing balloon angioplasty for coarctation will require subsequent surgical repair: A.
In newborns the ductal tissue recoils, so dilation gives only temporary relief, and surgery (resection with extended end-to-end anastomosis) is preferred.
Balloon dilation works well for recurrent coarctation after surgery, with lasting relief in most and restenosis in a minority; aneurysms after dilation occur in a few percent.
Recoarctation after neonatal surgical repair occurs in roughly 10 percent.
In the picture, six of the ten balloon-stretched newborn orcas go on to the surgeon's table.
Memory hook: a balloon in a newborn, the surgeon later in six of ten.
